The story relies heavily on well-worn romantic drama clichés and tropes. The overarching plot—two estranged lovers meeting awkwardly at a café to navigate unspoken feelings—is a staple of the genre. Furthermore, the text uses several overused literary devices and expressions to convey tension, such as commenting on the same old coat, sitting at "their" usual table by the window, remembering how the other takes their coffee ("Black. Without sugar."), looking out the window right as it starts to rain, and using "cold coffee" as a metaphor for their cooled relationship, followed by ordering a fresh, warm cup to symbolize a potential new beginning. Because these elements are so familiar and predictable, the piece cannot be considered entirely free of clichés.
